actions._comment: Scan the Data Privacy Center, not the home-page search funnel.
Two near-identical forms on the page. Scope everything to the removal form, which is the one with the success-styled submit button.
The removal form's select lists 19 states, but the search API answers for all of them. Add the rest so fillForm can pick the user's state.
Results list on a hit, status banner on a miss.

The location cell is a street address, so addressFull and not addressCityState. Rows have no link or id, and a hash identifier drops the street, so every namesake in one city would share one identifier. The location text as profileUrl gives each row its own.
The removal form's select lists 19 states, but the search API answers for all of them. Add the rest so fillForm can pick the user's state.
Re-search from userProfile. An extracted profile carries name as one string, so first and last name selectors fail against it.
Mark the row this job's extracted profile came from. A profileMatch on the user profile scores every namesake in the city the same and always picks the first row.
Wait for the widget iframe, not the empty container it mounts into.
The email field is optional so there is no generateEmail. The captcha is not optional.
